title: Nitrogen‐transforming microorganisms potentially facilitate the invasion of Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis) into evergreen broadleaf forests
content:
Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.


Abstract

Moso bamboo (Phyllostachys edulis) invasions into broadleaf forests can cause serious ecological problems, such as reducing biodiversity and disrupting community succession. An elevated soil NH4 +/NO3 − ratio has been identified as a potential mechanism that facilitates Moso bamboo invasion. However, it remains unclear whether and how this change is the result of the modification of soil nitrogen-transforming microorganisms by bamboo. Here, we collected soil from evergreen broadleaf forests that were either uninvaded or heavily invaded by Moso bamboo. We then compared the effects of soil origin on: (1) the growth of two common broadleaf tree species, Castanopsis fissa and Schima superba; (2) the soil nitrogen content and nitrogen transformation rates; and (3) the key microbial functional genes involved in nitrogen fixation, nitrification and denitrification. The plant sizes and relative growth rates of the study trees were significantly lower when they were grown in soil from the bamboo-invaded forest than when they were grown in the uninvaded forest, with values reduced by approximately half. Compared with uninvaded soil, bamboo-invaded soil presented a significantly greater denitrification rate, NH4 +-N content and NH4 +/NO3 − ratio. Further correlation analyses suggested that the increased diversity of denitrifying genes and altered community compositions of denitrifying microbes might be the drivers of the elevated NH4 +/NO3 − ratio, which consequently led to the reduced growth of broadleaf trees. Our study offers the first comprehensive synthesis of the positive feedback mechanisms of Moso bamboo invasion, with a focus on the instrumental role of nitrogen transformation processes.

摘要

毛竹(Phyllostachys edulis)入侵阔叶林会导致严重的生态问题，包括降低生物多样性和破坏群落演替等。土壤中NH4 +/NO3 −比值升高被认为是促进毛竹入侵的潜在机制。然而，目前尚不清楚是否是由于竹子入侵改变了土壤氮转化微生物群落而导致了这种土壤氮养分的变化和阔叶树种受到的负面影响。 在本研究中，我们采集了来自未被入侵或被毛竹严重入侵的常绿阔叶林的土壤并比较了土壤来源对以下方面的影响:(1)两种常见阔叶树种——黧蒴锥(Castanopsis fissa)和木荷(Schima superba)的生长情况；(2)土壤氮含量和氮转化速率；(3)参与固氮、硝化和反硝化过程的关键微生物功能基因。 与未被入侵的土壤相比，在毛竹入侵的土壤中生长的阔叶树在植株大小和相对生长速率方面都呈现显著降低的现象，数值大约减少了一半。毛竹入侵的土壤表现出显著更高的反硝化速率、NH4 +-N含量和NH4 +/NO3 −比值。进一步的相关性分析表明，反硝化基因多样性的增加和反硝化微生物群落组成的改变可能是导致NH4 +/NO3 −比值升高的驱动因素，这进而导致了阔叶树生长受抑制。 本研究首次系统探讨了毛竹入侵的正反馈机制，强调了氮转化过程的关键影响。
